### Background

NATS is an open source messaging system for cloud, on-premises and edge deployments.

JetStream permits authorized users to purge messages from a stream, including by subject and sequence.

### Problem Description

For memory-backed streams, some purge operations could perform work according to a supplied sequence bound rather than the messages actually present. An authorized purge request could hold the stream’s storage lock and consume excessive CPU, blocking operations on that stream and degrading server availability.

### Affected Versions

The issue is fixed in v2.14.10 and v2.15.3. Earlier versions containing the affected functionality are vulnerable; the first affected version has not been established for this notice.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-rr37-7hx9-8xw5>
 * Credit: @kalash33
repo.summary: Memory-backed stream purges can cause excessive CPU use
